title: finding: the tenant-scope index is declared on FEDERATED objects, where the wall composes no predicate and no DDL is ever issued — the #8608 disagreement's mirror image
body:
Restart-when: any PR makes provisionTenantScopeIndex in packages/objectql/src/registry.ts read injected-column provenance (#7865 convergence map resumes), or a gate begins pinning /meta/object/:name index accuracy

Observed while implementing #8608 (rebinding the tenant-scope index to the wall's derivation). Filed as an observation, **not fixed** — it is a divergence in the opposite direction from the one that card ruled on, it is pre-existing, and #8608's ruling was explicitly about granting the index where the wall applies, not withholding it where the wall does not.

## Measured

`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `applySystemFields` on an ADR-0015 `external` object carrying the registry's own injected anchor, `multiTenant: true`:

```
{ name: 'ext_customer', external: { remoteName: 'customers' }, fields: { name: ... } }
  =>  indexes: [{"fields":["organization_id"]}]
```

The same on the pre-#8608 tree — `external` is not one of the injection plan's opt-out rows, so `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(...).tenant` was already `true` there. **This card's finding is not introduced by #8608 and is not changed by it.**

## Why that entry appears to serve nothing

Two independent facts, both already established in the repo:

- **The wall composes no predicate on it.** #7835 established that a federated object's injected `organization_id` is a *phantom anchor*: `hasPhantomTenantAnchor` marks it, `computeTenantLayer0Filter` answers `objectHasOrgIdField: false`, and Layer 0 contributes nothing. Pinned in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/federated-tenant-layer0.test.ts`.
- **No DDL is ever issued for it.** `Engine.syncObjectSchema` returns early when `obj.external != null` (registers read metadata, no `syncSchema` call), so no index is created on any table — the remote schema is owned externally.

So the declared entry is inert metadata: an index that does not exist, cannot be created by us, and would serve a predicate that is never composed. It is still **served** on `/meta/object/:name` (the materialization seam stamps it), which is the part that may matter — a federated object reports an index the platform neither has nor can build, which is the "declared but not delivered" shape Prime Directive #10 names.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

#8608's ruling is "the index follows the wall" — read strictly, that sentence withholds here, because the wall composes nothing. But:

- the change is a **narrowing** on a surface no gate or test currently pins, and the card that just landed was scoped to widening one row;
- the observable harm is bounded to metadata accuracy — no missing index, no slow query, no isolation gap — so severity judged at filing time is genuinely uncertain in both directions;
- an author who declares a **real** remote `organization_id` on a federated object keeps a working wall (#7835's provenance half) and should keep any index question with it, so a naive `external != null` withholding would be wrong. Whatever fix lands has to read provenance, exactly as `hasPhantomTenantAnchor` does.

That last point is the reason this is worth recording rather than dropping: the correct predicate here is provenance-aware, and provenance is precisely what `carriesTenantScopeColumn` deliberately stopped reading in #8459.

## Suggested disposition

Triage as either (a) a metadata-accuracy repair in `provisionTenantScopeIndex` gated on `unprovisionedInjectedColumns` / `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance` (the machine-readable marker #7865 minted for exactly this), or (b) a deliberate no-op documented at the seam so the next reader does not re-derive the question. Either way it belongs on the #7865 convergence map beside #8608's entry.

Related: #8608 · #8459 · #7835 (phantom anchors) · #7865 (the convergence map) · #6810 · ADR-0015
